jamie: Urgent advisory 1: our container image scanner (build-bot) flagged secrets embedded in three images pushed to the staging registry during last night's pipeline run. No production pulls yet, but we need owners to remediate immediately.
build-bot: Automated alert: image redwood/staging/service-x:2026-03-22 contained 2 high-entropy strings matching AWS key patterns. image redwood/staging/worker-y:2026-03-22 and redwood/staging/etl-z:2026-03-22 had potential private key blobs. Full report: https://go/reports/container-secret-1792004321
jamie: Action items (owners & service account managers):
1) Revoke any long-lived credentials that may be exposed. For AWS keys run:
```bash
aws iam list-access-keys --user-name SERVICE_USER
aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id <KEY> --status Inactive
```
2) Rotate credentials and re-deploy images after rebuild with secrets removed.
3) Check image layers: run local scanner and confirm no secrets:
```bash
gcrctl image scan --image redwood/staging/service-x:2026-03-22 --rules secret
```
4) If your CI injects secrets into build-time env, move to ephemeral secret injection (runtime mounts or short-lived tokens). See migration guide: https://go/devex/ci-secret-best-practices

owen: Which teams pulled these images? Any downstream effects?

jamie: Staging only. No production deploys found in registry logs. We scanned recent deploys and didn't find production tags referencing these images. Still, treat as high priority.

tess: For the images that have embedded private keys, do we need to rotate TLS certs too?

jamie: If the key material maps to TLS/private key usage, yes rotate and reissue certs. If it's an API key, rotate that API key. If you're unsure, follow the quick triage steps in the report.

sec-bot: Summary: 3 images with findings. 2 service accounts with static keys older than 90 days referenced in logs. Scheduled automated revocation run at 1792011521 (8h) for any keys we confirmed exposed. Owners can preempt by revoking now.

ci-admin: CI owners 1: make sure build logs do not leak secrets. Remove any printed env vars. If your pipeline uploads images to the registry from forked PRs, add validation to block if secret patterns found.

owen: Is there a recommended quick patch for pipelines to block accidental secret bake-in?

ci-admin: Add a pre-push hook or job step using git-secrets or truffleHog-lite; example quick step:
```yaml
- name: Scan for secrets
  run: trufflehog --entropy=False --regex --max-depth 5 .
```
We can paste a ready-to-add snippet for common CI templates.

jamie: Owners: once you've revoked/rotated and rebuilt images, post confirmation here with the new image tag and rotated key IDs (redact full keys). We'll mark the ticket resolved. If you need help with rebuilds or secret scanning, ping @ci-admin or escalate to infra oncall.

tess: Acknowledged, starting remediation for worker-y. Will update in this thread when done.

jamie: Thanks. We're treating this as priority P1 until all three images are rebuilt and affected keys rotated. If you hit blockers, DM me. :warning:
